title: Capacity and Volume: Millilitres and Litres
seo_title: Grade 4 Capacity and Volume Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Estimate, measure, record, compare and order capacity of objects by measuring in millilitres and litres, using spoons, cups and measuring jugs; calculate and solve problems involving capacity/volume; convert between ml and ℓ (limited to whole numbers and common fractions).
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 4 capacity and volume worksheets: reading measuring jugs, millilitres and litres, converting, comparing and problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Read the jug at eye level.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Capacity is how much a container can hold. Volume is how much space something takes up.
  • We measure in millilitres (mℓ) and litres (ℓ). 1 000 mℓ = 1 ℓ.
  • A teaspoon holds about 5 mℓ, a cup about 250 mℓ, and a big cooldrink bottle 2 ℓ.
  • Read a measuring jug at eye level, at the top of the liquid.

Examples

Example

4 cups of 250 mℓ

4 × 250 = 1 000 mℓ

Answer: 1 ℓ

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Wrong markFind what each mark on the jug is worth.
100 mℓ in a litre1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ.
Mixing unitsChange ℓ to mℓ before adding.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 4 say about capacity?
faq.a: Estimate, measure, record, compare and order capacity using spoons, cups and measuring jugs, in millilitres and litres, and convert between ml and ℓ.

faq.q: How many cups make a litre?
What is the difference between capacity and volume?
faq.a: Capacity is what a container can hold; volume is the space taken up.
Looking from above or below gives a wrong reading.

items.q: A jug has a line every 250 mℓ. How many spaces are there from 0 up to 1 ℓ?
items.e: 1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ. Count by 250: 250, 500, 750, 1 000. That is 4 spaces. Do not count the 0 line as a space.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mℓ. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 mℓ ÷ 4 = 50 mℓ. Count the spaces after 200 mℓ: 250 mℓ, 300 mℓ, 350 mℓ. So it is 350 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mℓ. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 mℓ ÷ 4 = 50 mℓ. Count the spaces after 600 mℓ: 650 mℓ. So it is 650 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mℓ. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 mℓ ÷ 5 = 50 mℓ. Count the spaces after 250 mℓ: 300 mℓ, 350 mℓ, 400 mℓ. So it is 400 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mℓ. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 mℓ ÷ 5 = 50 mℓ. Count the spaces after 750 mℓ: 800 mℓ, 850 mℓ. So it is 850 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 mℓ. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 mℓ ÷ 4 = 25 mℓ. Count the spaces after 100 mℓ: 125 mℓ, 150 mℓ, 175 mℓ. So it is 175 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 mℓ. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 mℓ ÷ 4 = 25 mℓ. Count the spaces after 300 mℓ: 325 mℓ. So it is 325 mℓ.

items.q: The water is halfway between two lines. How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mℓ with 2 spaces, so each line is 100 mℓ. The water is halfway between 500 mℓ and 600 mℓ. Halfway is 550 mℓ.

items.q: The water is halfway between two lines. How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mℓ with 2 spaces, so each line is 100 mℓ. The water is halfway between 200 mℓ and 300 mℓ. Halfway is 250 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1 000 ÷ 4 = 250 mℓ. The water is 1 line above 1 ℓ: 1 × 250 = 250 mℓ. So it is 1 ℓ 250 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1 000 ÷ 4 = 250 mℓ. The water is 3 lines above 1 ℓ: 3 × 250 = 750 mℓ. So it is 1 ℓ 750 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 10 spaces, so each line is 1 000 ÷ 10 = 100 mℓ. The water is 4 lines above 1 ℓ: 4 × 100 = 400 mℓ. So it is 1 ℓ 400 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 2 spaces, so each line is 1 000 ÷ 2 = 500 mℓ. The water is 1 line above 2 ℓ: 1 × 500 = 500 mℓ. So it is 2 ℓ 500 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1 000 ÷ 4 = 250 mℓ. The water is 3 lines above 2 ℓ: 3 × 250 = 750 mℓ. So it is 2 ℓ 750 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 5 spaces, so each line is 1 000 ÷ 5 = 200 mℓ. The water is 3 lines up from the bottom: 3 × 200 = 600 mℓ. It has not reached 1 ℓ.

items.q: 34 ℓ = ☐ mℓ
items.e: 34 of 1 000 mℓ = 1 000 ÷ 4 × 3 = 750 mℓ.
8 000 mℓ = 8 ℓ, with 775 mℓ left: 8 ℓ 775 mℓ.
6 000 mℓ = 6 ℓ, with 895 mℓ left: 6 ℓ 895 mℓ.

items.q: How many litres are in 9 000 mℓ?

items.e: 5 000 mℓ = 5 ℓ, with 155 mℓ left: 5 ℓ 155 mℓ.

items.q: Which fact about capacity is true?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth, so 1 000 millilitres make 1 litre.

items.q: Which holds more: 4 ℓ or 4 500 mℓ?
items.e: 4 ℓ = 4 000 mℓ. 4 500 mℓ is more than 4 000 mℓ.

items.q: Half of a litre is how many millilitres?
items.e: 1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ. Half of 1 000 is 500, so half a litre is 500 mℓ.

items.q: 6 ℓ = ☐ mℓ
3 ℓ = ☐ mℓ
A teaspoon holds about how much?
items.e: A teaspoon is a good benchmark for 5 mℓ. 500 mℓ is half of a 1 ℓ carton of milk.

items.q: Which holds more: 2 ℓ or 1 900 mℓ?
items.e: 2 ℓ = 2 000 mℓ. 2 000 mℓ is more than 1 900 mℓ, so 2 ℓ is more. Compare in the same unit.

items.q: 10 ℓ = ☐ mℓ
1 ℓ 250 mℓ = ☐ mℓ
4 ℓ 80 mℓ = ☐ mℓ
items.e: 4 ℓ = 4 000 mℓ. Add the 80 mℓ: 4 000 + 80 = 4 080 mℓ. Keep the 0 in the hundreds place.
2,5 ℓ is 2 ℓ and half a litre (5 tenths). 2 000 mℓ + 500 mℓ = 2 500 mℓ.

items.q: How many millilitres are in 1 litre?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth. So 1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mℓ. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 mℓ. The water is 1 line above 200: 200 + 100 = 300 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mℓ. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 mℓ. The water is 1 line above 600: 600 + 100 = 700 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mℓ. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 mℓ. The water is 1 line above 800: 800 + 100 = 900 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mℓ. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 500 ÷ 2 = 250 mℓ. The water is 1 line up from the bottom: 250 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mℓ. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 500 ÷ 2 = 250 mℓ. The water is 1 line above 500: 500 + 250 = 750 mℓ.

items.q: About how much does a teaspoon hold?
items.e: A teaspoon holds about 5 millilitres. 500 mℓ is about a big bottle of water.

items.q: About how much does a can of fizzy drink hold?
items.e: A can of drink holds about 330 millilitres, which is about one third of a litre.

items.q: Convert. 6 ℓ = ☐ mℓ
items.e: 1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so you need more millilitres: multiply. 6 × 1 000 = 6 000, so 6 ℓ = 6 000 mℓ.

items.q: Convert. 7 000 mℓ = ☐ ℓ
items.e: 1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so you need fewer litres: divide. 7 000 ÷ 1 000 = 7, so 7 000 mℓ = 7 ℓ.

items.q: Convert. 1 ℓ 750 mℓ = ☐ mℓ
items.e: 1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ. Add the 750 mℓ: 1 000 + 750 = 1 750 mℓ. 850 mℓ would mean 1 ℓ = 100 mℓ, which is wrong.

items.q: Which is the same as 4 080 mℓ?
items.e: 4 000 mℓ = 4 ℓ. 4 080 mℓ = 4 ℓ and 80 mℓ left over (not 800 mℓ: the 8 is in the tens place).

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mℓ. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 250 ÷ 5 = 50 mℓ. The water is 3 lines above 250 mℓ: 250 + 150 = 400 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in litres and millilitres.
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mℓ. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 mℓ. The water is 3 lines above 1 000 mℓ: 1 000 + 300 = 1 300 mℓ. 1 000 mℓ = 1 ℓ, so 1 300 mℓ = 1 ℓ 300 mℓ.

items.q: Convert 3 ℓ to mℓ.
How many litres are in 4 000 mℓ?

items.e: 2 000 mℓ = 2 ℓ, with 430 mℓ left: 2 ℓ 430 mℓ.

items.q: 12 ℓ = ☐ mℓ
items.e: 12 of 1 000 mℓ = 1 000 ÷ 2 = 500 mℓ.

items.q: Convert 6 ℓ to mℓ.
How many litres are in 7 000 mℓ?
How many litres are in 5 000 mℓ?

items.e: 7 000 mℓ = 7 ℓ, with 240 mℓ left: 7 ℓ 240 mℓ.

items.q: How many litres are in 6 000 mℓ?

items.e: 1 000 mℓ = 1 ℓ, with 615 mℓ left: 1 ℓ 615 mℓ.

items.q: Convert 6 ℓ 755 mℓ to mℓ.
Convert 6 ℓ 931 mℓ to mℓ.
What is the best estimate for how much a teaspoon holds?
items.e: A teaspoon holds only a little, about 5 millilitres. 5 ℓ would fill a big bucket halfway.

items.q: What is the best estimate for how much a mug holds?
items.e: A mug of tea is about 300 millilitres. 300 ℓ would fill a bath.

items.q: What is the best estimate for how much a bucket holds?
items.e: A bucket holds about 10 litres. 10 mℓ is only two teaspoons.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 mℓ. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 mℓ. The water is 1 line above 200: 200 + 50 = 250 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 mℓ. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 mℓ. The water is 1 line above 300: 300 + 50 = 350 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 mℓ. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 mℓ. The water is 1 line above 400: 400 + 50 = 450 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mℓ. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 250 ÷ 5 = 50 mℓ. The water is 1 line above 500: 500 + 50 = 550 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mℓ. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 250 ÷ 5 = 50 mℓ. The water is 2 lines above 750: 750 + 100 = 850 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mℓ. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 mℓ. The water is 3 lines above 1 ℓ: 1 ℓ + 300 mℓ = 1 ℓ 300 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mℓ. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 mℓ. The water is 2 lines above 1 ℓ 500 mℓ: 1 ℓ 500 mℓ + 200 mℓ = 1 ℓ 700 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 2 equal spaces. 1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ, so each line is 1 000 ÷ 2 = 500 mℓ. The water is 1 line above 3 ℓ: 3 ℓ + 500 mℓ = 3 ℓ 500 mℓ.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 2 equal spaces. 1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ, so each line is 1 000 ÷ 2 = 500 mℓ. The water is 1 line above 1 ℓ: 1 ℓ + 500 mℓ = 1 ℓ 500 mℓ.

items.q: How much more water is needed to fill the jug to 500 mℓ?
items.e: Each line is 50 mℓ, so the water is at 150 mℓ. 500 − 150 = 350 mℓ more.

items.q: Pieter pours 250 mℓ of water out of the jug. How much is left?
items.e: The water is at 800 mℓ. Water is poured out, so subtract: 800 − 250 = 550 mℓ.
